empirical_power.limit: The inspected effect and dependence are uncertain. Neither this resampling nor the normal approximation predicts the years needed in a future market.

settings.effect_rule: The nonzero value is the inspected v1 point estimate, used only as a conditional planning scenario; I also retain the null.
settings.method: resample contiguous circular stationary blocks from the centred empirical series, add the fixed shift and record reference-method rejection
settings.scope: Resampling an observed history cannot reveal unseen persistence or forecast future power.
settings.source: v1 HAR+DVOL minus HAR loss differences

29.limit: HLN is a reference correction; persistent losses, nested models and generated forecasts can invalidate its nominal size.

59.limit: HLN is a reference correction; persistent losses, nested models and generated forecasts can invalidate its nominal size.

subsampling.limit: Subsampling is a candidate diagnostic. Its asymptotic assumptions and finite-sample calibration are not guaranteed by choosing a block rule.

mcs.scope: I report the surviving set as a diagnostic conditional on this inspected candidate set and dependence assumptions, not as proof of a best model.

settings.scope: I report the surviving set as a diagnostic conditional on this inspected candidate set and dependence assumptions, not as proof of a best model.

phases.scope: All phases reuse the same history. Favourable counts are a dependent stability display; no binomial test or independence claim applies.

specification.availability: I use features available at the origin and only labels with target_end_ms <= feature_cutoff_ms. Every fitted training row precedes the current origin.

bates_granger.interpretation: This is a nonnegative minimum-MSE Bates-Granger-style combination; its fitted weight has estimation risk and its objective differs from QLIKE.
bates_granger.vintages: Each past HAR component is reconstructed using only its own completed 365-label window. I estimate the current weight from the latest 365 such forecasts whose targets have ended.
bates_granger.weight: w_HAR = clip((mean(e_dvol^2) - mean(e_har*e_dvol)) / mean((e_har-e_dvol)^2), 0, 1); use 0.5 if denominator <= float64 epsilon times max(mean(e_har^2), mean(e_dvol^2), float64 tiny)

specification.cohort_reason: The retained cases cannot supply 730 completed labels in January 2023. The July start also allows 365 completed genuine vintage HAR forecasts for combination weights.

dm_hln.reference: Student t with n-1 degrees of freedom after HLN correction
dm_hln.scope: I report diagnostic p-values, including nested-model and generated-forecast limitations; they do not license significance claims.

ewma.forecast: next daily conditional variance held constant over 30 days, annualised by 365

specification.exploratory_focus: qlike_har_dvol minus qlike_har on the matched v2 cohort
specification.floor_scope: I apply the floor only to level-OLS HAR, HAR+DVOL and MZ forecasts and retain raw values and hit counts. Positive log-link, smearing, EWMA, GARCH and combination forecasts fail on nonpositive or nonfinite output rather than using this floor.

garch.annualisation: 365 * mean(next 30 conditional daily variances in percent-return units) / 100**2; simulation paths are averaged for EGARCH
garch.egarch_monte_carlo_check: I score the first fixed-seed batch and report its path-mean Monte Carlo standard error and the relative gap to an independent second batch of 2000 paths; I do not choose the lower-loss batch.
garch.failure: I retain convergence failures without selecting alternative starts.
garch.origin_seed: seed + origin_ms // 86400000; independent second batch adds 10000000

specification.inspection_history: I have already seen the reviewer's corrected strict-window means on the May 2023 cohort. The rebuilt window comparison is a replication of an inspected sensitivity, not an unseen test.

log_har.back_transform: exp(current fitted log variance) times mean(exp(training log residual))
log_har.interpretation: Training smearing supplies the in-sample QLIKE-optimal scalar. I do not assume Gaussian residuals or claim conditional unbiasedness.
log_har.regression: OLS log target on intercept and log daily, weekly and monthly RV; the augmented row adds log DVOL variance
log_har.standardisation: training feature means and standard deviations only

specification.matching: I retain every scheduled origin, all model failures and exclusions. Rankings and MCS use the intersection where every declared model succeeds; I report its size and each model's own coverage. I do not compare a restricted-cohort mean with a v1 full-cohort mean.

mcs.scope: I report the surviving set as a diagnostic conditional on this inspected candidate set and dependence assumptions, not as proof of a best model.

mz_dvol.fit: OLS actual variance on intercept plus raw DVOL variance over 730 completed labels
mz_dvol.floor_hits: I report every raw negative prediction and floor hit.
mz_dvol.forecast: max(positive_floor, fitted intercept + fitted slope * current DVOL variance)

specification.optional_data: I assess ETH, 5-minute RV and a VIX sanity check separately. I do not download or pool them under this BTC declaration.
specification.phases: I report all 30 phase means, counts and range. A count of favourable phases is a dependent stability display, not 30 independent replications or a binomial test.

power.effect_rule: The nonzero value is the inspected v1 point estimate, used only as a conditional planning scenario; I also retain the null.
power.method: resample contiguous circular stationary blocks from the centred empirical series, add the fixed shift and record reference-method rejection
power.scope: Resampling an observed history cannot reveal unseen persistence or forecast future power.
power.source: v1 HAR+DVOL minus HAR loss differences

specification.prospective_scope: I preserve the v1 locks, cohort, missing rule and disabled formal inference. This declaration does not activate a new prospective test.

qlike.failure: I retain nonconvergence or nonpositive/nonfinite forecasts as model failures. I do not replace them with a better-scoring fallback.
qlike.interpretation: The positive log link and objective differ from level OLS, so this comparison cannot isolate estimation noise alone.
qlike.optimizer: scipy L-BFGS-B; analytic gradient; initial intercept log(mean target), other coefficients zero

specification.reporting: I publish every declared model, failure, inference diagnostic and planning scenario, whichever way it goes. I do not pick specifications or block lengths by their result.
specification.role: I fix these additions after inspecting v1 and the independent review, before evaluating the additions. Every historical result remains exploratory.

subsampling.scope: I test finite-sample calibration before describing this as better calibrated. Fixed block fractions are not treated as an automatic repair.
subsampling.statistic: sqrt(block_size) * (block mean - full mean); compare its 2.5% and 97.5% quantiles with sqrt(n) * full mean

specification.vintage: I reuse the retained BTC vintage. I do not refresh it for this comparison.

window_check_cohort.role: I separately rebuild the strict matched-window comparison supplied in the review clarification. I do not compare these means with the full v1 cohort.

specification.window_scope: The 365, 730 and expanding sensitivities apply to level HAR and HAR+DVOL. Log, QLIKE and MZ fits use 730 completed 30-day labels. EWMA, GARCH and EGARCH use 730 daily midnight-to-midnight log returns available through the feature cutoff. Bates-Granger uses 365 completed genuine HAR365 forecast vintages.
